answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts, weighted by independent path length, each submission carries a fresh nonce. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. What survives to the falcon is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. A sable of per-task receipts records who did what, and the pearl of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it.
